environments.local: https://wbcom-free.local - WP 6.9.1, BuddyPress 14.x, BuddyX theme. HTTPS on purpose (ALTCHA needs a secure context).
environments.pristine: docker-smoke bn-docker-smoke-* at http://localhost:8896 - WP 7.0.2, PHP 8.3, installed FROM THE BUILT ZIP alongside Sensei/LifterLMS/Reign.

A: A1 fresh activation on the pristine install: active at 2.2.0, front page/wp-login/REST all 200, and with NO keys configured login still succeeds - an unconfigured CAPTCHA never locks anyone out
A2 no tables created; RFB_PLUGIN_VERSION, header, readme Stable tag and package.json all 2.2.0
A3 GET /wp-json/altcha/v1/challenge -> 200; rest-reachability: 1 route, permission-gated, no 5xx
C: login-form-surfaces: end-to-end login through a core Login/Logout block for ALL FIVE services, widget confirmed inside the <form>
register: BuddyPress signup completed in one pass on reCAPTCHA v3, wp_signups row confirmed
lost-password + comment: widget renders on both, and each blocks an unsolved submit
toggles-enforce: comment and wp_lostpassword verified ON (blocks) and OFF (allows) - no dead toggles
ip-allowlist: allowlisted client gets no widget AND logs in; non-allowlisted still blocked
unconfigured: pristine install shows the 'missing API keys' notice and leaves forms submittable
admin settings: all tabs render clean on both environments, including at it_IT
mobile: admin Advanced tab at 390px, 0px horizontal overflow
D: all ten D rows verified - see AGENT_SMOKE_RUNBOOK.md section D
E: all five providers rendered and completed a real login: recaptcha-v2, recaptcha-v3 (real keys, 2105-char token), turnstile, hcaptcha, altcha (over https)

manual_required: B upgrade path: not run. Install 2.1.0 first, configure it, upgrade to 2.2.0 and diff every wbc_* option before/after. WBC_Settings_Migration rewrites key spellings, so a dropped key could silently disarm or lock out a live site.
C.anon.wp-login: wp-login.php itself was verified by render assertion, not by driving the form in a browser. The wp_login_form() surfaces WERE driven end-to-end.

C.anon.ajax-login: the plugin's own AJAX login widget (#wbc-ajax-login-form, context widget_login) was not exercised in the browser. It shares the v3 bootstrap that was broken, so it is likely fixed, but that is inference.

E full matrix: only the login-block context was run across all five providers. WooCommerce, EDD, MemberPress, Ultimate Member and the seven form-builder contexts were not run at all - those plugins are not installed locally.
F: Firefox and Safari iOS not run.
Front-end 390px: only the admin was checked at mobile width.
notes: Truthful report, not a rubber stamp. Section counts reflect what was actually executed; everything not executed is listed in manual_required rather than counted as a pass. The only debug.log line on the pristine install was a WP_DEBUG-level note ('Active captcha service is not configured'), which is intended behaviour, not a warning.
